run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:11:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans: the value the alert reports at its start instant (0.02222222222222222 at 2026-11-16T14:11:49Z) is exactly the 2-minute rate of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for frontend-proxy, and that value comes entirely from span_name="ingress" (0.0222) while "router frontend egress" was 0 at that instant. The frontend-proxy access log shows those ingress errors are 503 responses with Envoy flag UC and reason upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} toward the upstream named "frontend", i.e. the frontend closed/reset the connection before sending a response; the same signature recurs throughout the window (13:49, 13:52, 13:53, 13:55, and 14:10:16-14:11:18 immediately before the alert started). A second, larger error episode in the same window (peaking 14:04-14:05) is a different path: the payment Deployment was explicitly restarted (kubectl restart annotation 14:02:11Z, old pod killed 14:02:14Z, same image), payment served no 'charge' spans for roughly 2-3 minutes, checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls errored, frontend's /api/checkout returned errors (~72.6 error spans in the 10 minutes to 14:12, 20.7% of PlaceOrder/POST spans) and frontend-proxy recorded matching egress+ingress errors. Frontend and payment pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts, no OOMKilled/Evicted, endpoints resolve to one pod each, and all nodes are Ready without pressure, so pod crash, eviction or node pressure are not supported. The exact reason the frontend terminates individual connections is not visible: the frontend container produced no readable stdout and its own spans carry no error status for those requests, and the Envoy configuration is not exposed in any otel-demo ConfigMap.

claims.text: At the alert's start time 2026-11-16T14:11:49Z, sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) evaluated to 0.02222222222222222, identical to the alert annotation's current value.

At the same instant the frontend-proxy error rate was composed only of span_name="ingress" (0.02222222222222222); span_name="router frontend egress" was exactly 0, so the value that made the alert fire came from ingress-side 503s, not from upstream-call failures.

frontend-proxy access logs record HTTP 503 with Envoy flag UC and reason upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} toward upstream "frontend" at 2026-11-16T14:10:16.051Z, 14:10:31.791Z, 14:11:04.826Z, 14:11:18.351Z, 14:14:02.816Z and 14:15:05.351Z (requests GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4, /api/cart, /api/data/?contextKeys=assembly, /api/data/?contextKeys=accessories, /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ, /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z; response body 95 bytes, upstream duration 116-844 ms).

The same 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} pattern toward upstream "frontend" occurs earlier in the window at 13:49:05.336Z, 13:49:05.679Z, 13:49:52.293Z, 13:52:45.273Z, 13:53:48.272Z and 13:55:05.321Z (upstream durations 43-1267 ms).

frontend-proxy ingress error-span rate was nonzero at many 2-minute points between 13:52 and 14:19 (0.0111-0.0275 errors/s at the 13:54, 13:55, 13:57, 14:00, 14:06, 14:09, 14:12, 14:13, 14:16, 14:17 and 14:18 points), whereas the "router frontend egress" error rate was nonzero only at the 14:04:00 point (0.3222/s) and the 14:05:00 point (0.4444/s).

In the sampled frontend-proxy error traces, the error rows are "ingress" spans carrying http.status_code="503", error=true and otel.status_code="ERROR", each with a child "router frontend egress" span carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0"; those traces contain load-generator and frontend-proxy spans but no span attributed to the frontend service.

Over the 75 minutes ending 14:28:16 frontend-proxy accumulated 89.2 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on "ingress" and 69.9 on "router frontend egress", against 26,232 and 26,249 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans respectively.
frontend-proxy's 5-minute error-span ratio peaked at 0.02531 (point 14:04:49) and 0.02505 (point 14:06:49), versus 0 to 0.00076 at the other points of the 13:42-14:20 series.
The frontend service's own 5-minute error-span ratio was exactly 0 at every sampled point except the same two points 14:04:49 (0.02353) and 14:06:49 (0.02379).

Among the frontend span names returned, only POST, POST /api/checkout, "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder carried error spans during the burst (0.3111/s at the 14:04 point and 0.4556/s at the 14:05 point); GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, GET /, render route, resolve page components, the product/recommendation routes and the AdService/CartService gRPC spans were 0 at those points.

In the 10 minutes ending 14:12:00 the frontend recorded 72.63 error spans each on grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, POST /api/checkout, "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" and POST, against 277.89 UNSET PlaceOrder spans and 277.89 UNSET POST /api/checkout spans, i.e. about 20.7% of those spans errored.

checkout's error spans occur only at the 14:05:00 point (0.45556 errors/s on each of oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, 0 at every other point of the 13:52-14:19 series); over 75 minutes those two span names accumulated 42.46 and 42.41 error spans.

payment's own "charge" span rate dropped to 0.0667/s at the 14:04:00 point and 0/s at the 14:05:00 point, against 0.30-0.56/s at every other point of the 13:52-14:19 series, and returned to 0.50/s at 14:06:00.

payment recorded no error-status spans in the window: span_name="charge" and "grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" each show 1341.78 spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect show STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 0.

Kubernetes events show the payment rollout: pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Scheduled/created/container started 14:02:11-14:02:14 with ReplicaSet/payment-54499f9786 SuccessfulCreate, old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 "Stopping container payment" (Killing) at 14:02:14 followed by ReplicaSet/payment-55766d76b9 SuccessfulDelete, and Deployment/payment ScalingReplicaSet up 0->1 and down 1->0; the same events query returned no event for any frontend or checkout object.

ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 (created 2026-11-16T14:02:11Z) carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt="2026-11-16T14:02:11Z" and the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment as the old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 (now 0 replicas), so this was an explicit restart rollout, not an image change.

Pod state at query time: frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt and payment-54499f9786-4r25d are Running with all containers ready, restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated reason (no OOMKilled/Evicted); start times are 13:29:59Z (frontend) and 14:02:11Z (payment).

The frontend and payment Services are ClusterIP on port 8080 -> targetPort 8080 and their Endpoints each contain exactly one address (frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt 100.96.5.121, payment-54499f9786-4r25d 100.96.5.201), both pods on node i-0e631601b68dd932a.
All 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False.

checkout logs between 14:06:44.757Z and 14:06:59.573Z show repeated successful checkout handling ("[PlaceOrder]", "payment went through", "order placed", "order confirmation email sent"), consistent with recovery after the burst.

The per-service error-spans series returned for this window cover accounting, ad, checkout, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment and recommendation; ad, recommendation and fraud-detection show only isolated single-error blips around 0.011/s on flagd EventStream spans at scattered points, and accounting stayed 0, none of which involve frontend-proxy.

Object-level frontend failure is not supported: frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt is Running and ready with restartCount 0, started 13:29:59Z, no lastState.terminated reason, and the events query for frontend objects returned nothing.

Node-level resource pressure and routing misconfiguration are not supported: all nodes are Ready with no memory/disk/PID pressure, and the frontend and payment Services/Endpoints resolve to a single healthy pod address each.

The payment restart burst was no longer contributing to the alert value at its start instant: at 14:11:49 the "router frontend egress" error rate was 0 and only "ingress" was nonzero (0.0222), while the egress/ingress burst had ended after the 14:05 point.

Rejected: that the alert is caused by frontend pod crashes, OOMKills or reschedules. The frontend pod has restartCount 0, no lastState.terminated reason, has been running since 13:29:59Z and has no events; the only pod replacement in the namespace during the window is payment's explicit rollout restart.
Rejected: that node resource pressure on the shared node i-0e631601b68dd932a explains the 503s. All nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

The 503s that hold the alert above 0 are produced because the frontend upstream of frontend-proxy terminates the HTTP/1.1 connection before a response is started (Envoy response flag UC, upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}) on individual GET /api/* requests; the requests that fail in the trace sample carry no frontend span and no frontend error status, so the frontend drops the connection without an application-level error being recorded.

The 14:02-14:05 error burst is explained by the payment Deployment restart: the old payment pod was killed at 14:02:14 and payment emitted no "charge" spans for roughly 2-3 minutes afterwards, so checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls failed and frontend's POST /api/checkout returned errors, which frontend-proxy recorded as matching egress (69.9) and ingress error spans. Timing and signal counts support this, but the checkout client's error text/gRPC status for Charge was not captured, so causation is not directly proven.

An alternative, unverified mechanism for the UC 503s is a connection-reuse/idle-timeout mismatch between frontend-proxy's upstream connection pool and the frontend server's keep-alive timeout; no frontend-proxy/Envoy configuration object exists in the otel-demo ConfigMaps (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products), so this could not be checked.

Compare frontend-proxy's upstream HTTP/1.1 idle/keep-alive and retry settings with the frontend server's keep-alive behaviour (the UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} signature on GET /api/* is typical of reuse of a connection the upstream is closing), and consider an Envoy retry policy for idempotent GETs.

Review the payment rollout restart of 2026-11-16T14:02:11Z: with a single replica and no serving traffic for roughly 2-3 minutes after the new pod started, checkout's Charge calls failed. Investigate why the replacement pod was not serving (readiness probe semantics, gRPC client reconnect backoff) and protect the rollout (surge/availability settings or a second replica).

gaps: Jaeger's newest trace at query time was 2026-11-16T13:57:41Z, so no traces exist for the 14:02-14:15 burst; the HTTP status frontend returned on /api/checkout and the gRPC status/deadline of checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls during that burst are unverified.

The frontend container produced no readable stdout/stderr lines in the queried windows (0 bytes read for 13:45-13:56 and 14:00-14:08), so the reason the frontend terminates connections cannot be confirmed from application logs.
No frontend-proxy/Envoy ConfigMap or config dump is exposed in otel-demo, so upstream idle timeouts, retry policy and connection-pool settings could not be verified.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who or what issued the kubectl restart at 2026-11-16T14:02:11Z and whether any other change occurred is unknown.

The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was not returned by the rules API (status no_data), so its exact expression, window and threshold are unverified; the match to sum(rate(...STATUS_CODE_ERROR[2m])) is inferred from the identical value 0.02222222222222222.

frontend-proxy log reads are bounded by a 4 MiB read limit and the stream only extended to 14:16:12Z at query time, so the count of UC 503s in the window is a sample, not a complete count, and nothing after 14:16:12Z is known.
No error-status series was returned for cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, email, quote or image-provider, so their state is unknown rather than verified healthy.
The old payment pod's logs and container state no longer exist, so whether it shut down cleanly or how long the new pod took to accept Charge traffic cannot be determined.

Two queries returned no data and prove nothing either way: the http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series is absent under service_name="frontend-proxy" (only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket exist), and error=true trace searches for the checkout and frontend services returned no traces while the same tags did match frontend-proxy.
next_steps: Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream connection settings with the frontend server's keep-alive timeout and consider enabling retries for idempotent GET requests.

Compare the frontend's readiness-probe semantics and the payment Deployment's rollout strategy (single replica, maxUnavailable/surge) to prevent the ~2-3 minute Charge-serving gap observed after the 14:02:11Z restart.
Consult change history (not integrated here) for the actor and intent of the payment kubectl restart at 2026-11-16T14:02:11Z.
Enable or verify frontend application logging/metrics so the connection-termination reason (UC) can be diagnosed from the upstream side.
